inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (plus VisualCoreTestSupport for tests). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio, VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For Shader Studio (checked 2026-11-17): VisualCoreShaderSource has ShaderLibrary, ExpandedShader with SourceOrigin, ShaderSourceError, InfoLogParser, ShaderDiagnostic and ShaderStage; VisualCoreRendering has ResourceRegistry.program, ShaderError, ShaderProgram (uniform reflection, typed setters, a global lastFailureLog), FullScreenShaderScene, ShaderBundle with the vc/ library, Texture.upload(rgba:), makeTexture, makeRenderTarget and RenderCapabilities; VisualCoreDiagnostics has ResourceBudget, PacingMeter, FramePacing, PerformanceRecord and the quality governor; VisualCoreParameters has ParameterDefinition, ParameterSchema and ParameterEditor; VisualCoreExperience has ExperienceStorage under StorageQuota and ExperienceSnapshot; VisualCorePersistence has MigrationChain, DocumentStore and NamedLibrary (on a raw directory). Missing in every framework product (grep 2026-11-17): a watchdog or frame-time budget for a slow shader and hang detection; a code editor, line-numbered text view or syntax assistance; a scene that swaps in a new program only on success and keeps the last good one; texture inputs for a full-screen shader; a library of named files over the experience storage; per-shader compile logs.

inventory.area: EGL render host and its main-thread rule
inventory.description: RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler paced by FramePacing and the context generations, and exposes capabilities (RenderCapabilities), resources (ResourceRegistry), replaceScene, pause, resume and recreateContext. RenderHost, ResourceRegistry, ShaderProgram, RenderScene and the presenter are main-actor: GL work happens only inside a scene's setup, resize, render and teardown with the host's context current, on the main thread (VisualCore has no other GL thread). The pure modules (shader source, parameters, persistence, diagnostics) are Sendable. A compile is therefore never run from a control's action: the action queues a request that the preview scene compiles at its next frame, one at a time, the newest replacing a waiting one (G-PREVIEW).

inventory.area: Shader source expansion, diagnostics, compile and link
inventory.description: ShaderLibrary expands #include and defines up to 64 KiB (maxExpandedBytes) at most 8 levels deep (maxIncludeDepth); it accepts only #version 300 es, inserts the version line when missing, adds no precision line and no #line, and records each expanded line's SourceOrigin (ExpandedShader.origin(ofExpandedLine:)); refusals are ShaderSourceError. InfoLogParser.parse(_:stage:map:) turns a compile or link log into [ShaderDiagnostic] (file, line, stage, severity, message; line only, no column) mapped to the original file and line. ResourceRegistry.program(vertex:fragment:defines:library:vertexName:fragmentName:) throws ShaderError.source, .compile([ShaderDiagnostic]) or .link([ShaderDiagnostic]); a failure never touches a program the caller holds; it keeps a 64-program LRU cache (maxCachedPrograms). ShaderProgram reads the active uniforms (name, type, size) and has typed setters; ShaderProgram.lastFailureLog is one global string and is not relied on.

inventory.area: Full-screen shaders and the GLSL library
inventory.description: FullScreenShaderScene draws one fragment shader over the canvas with u_time, u_resolution, u_seed, an 8-entry palette and one float per parameter; its source is fixed at creation, it keeps only the first diagnostic (errorMessage), it has no texture input, and a failure draws dark grey. ShaderBundle compiles bundled GLSL with #include of the vc/ library (noise, hash, palette, color, sdf, field). Fractal Explorer passes runtime fragment text to FullScreenShaderScene(fragment:fragmentName:bundle:) and Generative Art Studio builds its scenes in ArtSceneFactory; both stay experience code.

inventory.area: Textures, render targets and capability queries
inventory.description: ResourceRegistry.makeTexture (rgba8, rgba16f, r8) and Texture.upload(rgba:) upload pixels made in code; makeRenderTarget, acquireTarget, recycle, release and trimPools manage targets; ResourceRegistry.stats and ResourceBudget (256 MiB by default) bound GPU bytes. RenderCapabilities on RenderHost.capabilities reports the GL and GLSL versions, extensions, texture, viewport and uniform limits (maxFragmentUniformVectors, maxTextureImageUnits) and shader precisions (fragmentHighp, fragmentMantissaBits); the context is GLSL ES 3.00 only.

ParameterDefinition and ParameterSchema (at most 64, NaN refused, out of range clamped) and ParameterEditor model bounded values. ExperienceStorage.write(_:to:), read, list and remove work in the experience's own folder under StorageQuota (64 files, 16 MiB), with setValue(_:for:) for 64 small values of 4 KB; ExperienceSnapshot and MigrationChain version state. Digital Zen Garden's GardenLibrary (versioned envelopes, capped count and size, damaged and newer files refused and kept) is app-local and internal; VisualCorePersistence's DocumentStore and NamedLibrary work on a raw directory, not on the experience storage. FramePacing, PacingMeter (drawn-frame intervals: median, p95, p99, missed), PerformanceRecord and the presenter's maxFramesPerSecond pace and measure frames; no watchdog exists.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies quality (QualityGovernor over the QualityProfile with QualityPolicy, fed by DeviceConditions), memory-warning and scene-phase events and keeps a PerformanceRecord; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls, pointer input, canvas overlay, maxFramesPerSecond); ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state with its qualityTiers. The one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json: twenty-one registered (A01-A21), candidates empty (checked 2026-11-17); a22 appears in neither, AppModelTests uses it as a synthetic not-yet-integrated id, and Shader Studio stays unregistered and unavailable in A22-P00. The catalog lists it as free, family Developer and creator tools, launcher category tools.

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: python3 scripts/release_check.py --list prints 163 lines (2026-11-17): shared checks including app-contracts (every docs/apps/*/visualcore-contract.json), licenses and usage-descriptions; package and app builds and tests; experience-release and copy-claims steps of the released experiences; verify steps of A01-A21 on iOS 27 and 26; the release audits; the seven reference regression steps and the ProjectM independence check. No A22 step exists yet; they come with G-RELEASE.

Shader Studio owns its domain and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/ShaderStudio/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests; created in A22-P01, not present today): the project, template, uniform and diagnostic models; the source validator and its caps; line mapping; the starter templates over vc/; the preview scene with its queued compile requests and last-good swap; the editor, the diagnostics list and the parameter inspector; texture inputs made in code; the project library over ExperienceStorage; the watchdog, stop and reset; the compatibility profile view; copy. VisualCore owns reusable machinery: source expansion and diagnostics (VisualCoreShaderSource), compile, link, textures, targets and capabilities (VisualCoreRendering), pacing, quality and budgets (VisualCoreDiagnostics), parameters (VisualCoreParameters), persistence (VisualCorePersistence), storage, snapshots and the host (VisualCoreExperience, VisualCoreExperienceHost). Fractal Explorer's runtime fragment and Digital Zen Garden's GardenLibrary stay experience code and are not copied. ProjectM stays in the harness. No VisualCore change is planned.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in docs/apps/shader-studio/regression-baseline.md. Phase start for the no-change diff of Packages and External: 6218b9a1 (after the A22 constitution commit 27d7d83e).

gaps.justification: The project, template, uniform and diagnostic models are the experience's domain, pure and GPU-free in its Core (manual phase 01, research D4). No VisualCore change is planned (clarification Q3); a second user would justify moving them upstream (Principle II).
gaps.test: Core host tests: each model round-trips and migrates through MigrationChain; truncated, newer, NaN, infinite and out-of-range values are refused or clamped to the declared bounds; the digest is stable for the same inputs.

gaps.justification: The pre-compile caps (source bytes, lines, uniforms, inputs, preview size) are Shader Studio's policy; ShaderLibrary's 64 KiB expansion limit stays the hard ceiling (clarification Q4). The numbers are decided with their tests (research D4a).
gaps.test: Core host tests: sources at and one past each cap are accepted and refused with a named reason; no compile request is made for a refused source; empty, binary and non-UTF-8 text is refused.

gaps.justification: The template prefix (version, precision line, vc/ includes) is the experience's own; mapping diagnostics back to the person's lines over ExpandedShader.origin(ofExpandedLine:) is app-local (clarification Q3). Diagnostics stay line-only.
gaps.test: Core host tests: a known error on person line N in each template maps to line N after the prefix; diagnostics on prefix lines map to the template and never to a person line; a log without a line keeps the message.

gaps.justification: The starter templates over vc/ with their declared uniforms and texture inputs are experience content written in code (manual phase 01; visuals are code).
gaps.test: Core and experience tests: every template expands within the caps, declares only bounded uniforms and inputs, and compiles and links on the simulator host with no diagnostic.

gaps.justification: The preview scene compiles queued requests in the host's context at its next frame, one at a time with the newest replacing a waiting one, swaps programs only on success, keeps the last good program, binds uniforms from reflection and rebuilds from source after context loss. FullScreenShaderScene cannot replace its source and drops later diagnostics, so the swap is app-local with no VisualCore change (clarification Q3); a second user would justify moving it upstream.
gaps.test: Experience tests: a failing compile keeps drawing the last good program (read-back unchanged) and reports every diagnostic; two queued requests compile only the newest; at most one compile per frame; after recreateContext the last good program is rebuilt from source.

gaps.justification: The explicit Compile and Run action and its states (idle, queued, compiled, failed) are the experience's interface over the preview scene (manual phase 02).
gaps.test: Experience tests: Run queues exactly one request; a control never calls ResourceRegistry.program directly; a failed run shows the diagnostics and leaves the preview on the last good program.

gaps.justification: No code editor exists in VisualCore. A monospaced SwiftUI editor with line numbers, a diagnostics list that jumps to a line, syntax assistance, hardware-keyboard support and an iPad-first layout is app-local (clarification Q5; manual §13 risk 2).
gaps.test: Experience tests: line numbers match the text; selecting a diagnostic moves the cursor to its line; keyboard shortcuts for Run and next diagnostic work; the layout keeps editor and preview usable at iPhone and iPad sizes with Dynamic Type.

gaps.justification: The inspector binds bounded uniforms (ParameterSchema, ParameterEditor) to reflected uniforms (ShaderProgram.uniforms) of the person's program; the binding is experience logic (manual phase 03).
gaps.test: Experience tests: only declared, reflected float and vector uniforms appear; values are clamped to their bounds and NaN refused; a uniform missing after recompile is dropped without a crash.

gaps.justification: Small texture inputs generated in code and uploaded with Texture.upload(rgba:) in the preview scene are app-local; FullScreenShaderScene has no texture input (clarification Q5).
gaps.test: Experience tests: each generated input has the declared size and checksum, is bound to its sampler unit, stays within ResourceBudget and is rebuilt after context loss.

gaps.justification: Named, versioned project files over ExperienceStorage after Digital Zen Garden's GardenLibrary pattern (capped count and size, damaged and newer files refused and never deleted) are app-local; NamedLibrary works on a raw directory (research D6).
gaps.test: Experience tests: save, open, rename and remove round-trip; the count and size caps refuse with a message; damaged and newer files are refused and still present afterwards; StorageQuota is never exceeded.

gaps.justification: A watchdog over PacingMeter's drawn-frame intervals that stops the preview and offers a reset to the last good program is app-local; a VisualCore watchdog was rejected with one user (research D6). No sandbox is claimed.
gaps.test: Experience tests with injected intervals: frames slower than the limit for the declared window stop the preview; reset restores the last good program; recovery needs no relaunch; normal frames never trigger it.

gaps.justification: Driver behaviour of slow shaders, hardware keyboards and iPhone ergonomics can only be measured on the D1-D3 devices after ImplementationLock-100 (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
gaps.test: Device plan lists per device: a slow template stopped by the watchdog, a compile error mapped to the right line, a hardware-keyboard run and the compatibility profile; results recorded as device evidence only.

gaps.justification: Registration, the A22 release-check, copy-claims and verify steps, the license entries and the catalog availability are the experience's release work (manual phase 06).
gaps.test: Release check lists the A22 steps and passes; check_copy_claims.py finds no sandbox or unmeasured performance claim; Shader Studio is registered and available only after its release gate.

negative.rule: Risk 1, user GLSL triggers expensive driver behaviour. Owner: the source validator and its caps (app-local G-VALIDATE in A22-P01), the capped preview size and frame rate and the last good program (G-PREVIEW in A22-P02), the watchdog, stop and reset (G-WATCHDOG in A22-P04) and the device measurements (G-DEVICE in A22-P05). Verification: Core tests prove every cap refuses one past its limit before any compile; experience tests prove the preview never exceeds its size and 30 frames per second, and that injected slow frames stop it and reset restores the last good program; a copy scan finds no sandbox claim; the device campaign runs a slow template per device. Release blocker: a compile without the caps, a preview that cannot be stopped and reset, or any sandbox or isolation claim.

Risk 2, keyboard and editor ergonomics on iPhone. Owner: the editor with line numbers, diagnostics list and hardware-keyboard support, iPad first (app-local G-EDITOR in A22-P03) and the device journeys (G-DEVICE in A22-P05). Verification: experience tests prove line numbers, jump-to-line from a diagnostic and the keyboard shortcuts at iPhone and iPad sizes with Dynamic Type; the device campaign edits and runs a template with a hardware keyboard and on an iPhone. Release blocker: an editor without line numbers or diagnostics navigation, Run unreachable from the keyboard, or an iPhone layout where the editor or preview cannot be used.
